answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a refundable bond before trading, and its reputation grows only from completed, attested transactions over time. Fake identities then cost real capital per identity, and a single fraud can slash the bond, so creating thousands of sock puppets is expensive and unprofitable. Trust spreads through the transaction graph like a vine along a thread, branching slowly, while a willow bends but does not break under many weak claims because only staked, proven history counts.
